title: An orchestrator told its log's path overwrote the log, and the host's backup followed
foundBy: session agent, from a live dispatch viewer run against the task-tracker campaign tt-v18-run19
details:
In tt-v18-run19 the orchestrator wrote its own log with `cat > ~/.local/share/cs-campaign/output/log.jsonl`, which replaces the file. It wrote four lines in a format of its own, with invented minute-precision times. Then it ran `cs-campaign-member note assessment --file` on the log file itself. Its reasoning quotes the orientation: "Your log, ~/.local/share/cs-campaign/output/log.jsonl, holds your notes and acceptances", and decides "Let me keep a light log."

The log is the only record of acceptance, so the overwrite lost five acceptances. Three surveyors went back to `node-replied`, so the orchestrator had to accept them again. The modeller's d001 and d002 acceptances are gone from the record for good. `observe` copies the log to `<name>.log-mirror.jsonl` on the host, so the claim survives a lost machine, but it replaces the copy on every look. The backup is missing the same lines.

The orientation and the restart message name the file because a fresh session must read its log, and no tool reads it. Wanted: a member verb that prints the log, and texts that name that tool rather than the path. Also wanted: a `note` that refuses the log as its input, and a host copy that keeps every line it has seen.
